isomorphisms.name: Foundational Axiom Circularity
isomorphisms.chi_law: Each system's foundational axiom is self-validating and cannot be externally proven without undermining its own claim to ultimacy.
isomorphisms.physics_process: Gödel's incompleteness theorems: any sufficiently powerful formal system cannot prove its own consistency from within; it requires a meta-system, which itself has the same limitation.
isomorphisms.theological_phenomenon: Self-authentication of Scripture (Calvin) and divine aseity (God swears by Himself, Hebrews 6:13).
isomorphisms.prediction: Any foundational system will exhibit a similar circularity; no system can escape this structural constraint.
physics_process_steps: Formal system S is defined with axioms and inference rules.
S attempts to prove its own consistency using only its own axioms.
Gödel's second incompleteness theorem shows this is impossible if S is consistent and sufficiently expressive.
To prove consistency, a meta-system M is needed, which itself cannot prove its own consistency.
The limitation is structural, not a flaw in S.
mapped_text_steps: Scientific Naturalism assumes causal closure of the physical as an axiom.
It cannot prove this axiom using its own method (empirical science).
Biblical Theism assumes divine aseity and revelation as an axiom.
It cannot prove this axiom using an external authority without undermining its claim.
Both systems exhibit structural circularity; this is a feature of any foundational claim.
preserved_transitions: Axiom → self-validation → inability to externally prove → structural necessity
isomorphisms.notes: The mapping is nearly perfect. The only slight asymmetry is that Gödel's theorem applies to formal systems, while the text discusses epistemological systems. However, the structural parallel is exact.

isomorphisms.name: Presuppositional Requirements
isomorphisms.chi_law: Both systems require unprovable presuppositions before any knowledge claim can be made.
isomorphisms.physics_process: Measurement theory: any measurement requires a prior calibration standard that cannot itself be measured by the same instrument without circularity.
isomorphisms.theological_phenomenon: The necessity of faith (acceptance of unprovable starting point) for knowledge of God.
isomorphisms.prediction: Any knowledge system will have presuppositions that cannot be justified within the system.
physics_process_steps: Choose a measurement instrument (e.g., ruler).
To calibrate the ruler, you need a standard length.
That standard length cannot be measured by the same ruler without circularity.
The standard is accepted by convention or external authority.
mapped_text_steps: Science requires ten presuppositions (Gauch) it cannot test.
These include existence of external world, uniformity of nature, reliability of senses.
Theology requires faith in revelation as a starting point.
Neither can prove its presuppositions using its own method.
preserved_transitions: Need for foundation → acceptance of unprovable axiom → circular justification
isomorphisms.notes: The mapping is strong. The number of presuppositions differs (10 vs. 1-2), but the structural role is identical.

isomorphisms.name: Inductive vs. Scriptural Circularity
isomorphisms.chi_law: Both systems use a circular justification: the method validates itself by appealing to its own past success.
isomorphisms.physics_process: Self-consistency in dynamical systems: a system's future behavior is predicted by its past behavior, but the assumption of consistency is not derivable from the system itself.
isomorphisms.theological_phenomenon: Scripture attests to its own divine origin; the Holy Spirit confirms it to the believer (Calvin).
isomorphisms.prediction: Both circularities will be structurally isomorphic: past success justifies future trust, but the justification is circular.
physics_process_steps: Observe that induction has worked in the past.
Conclude that induction will work in the future.
This conclusion is itself an inductive argument.
The circularity is unavoidable.
mapped_text_steps: The Bible claims to be God's Word.
The Bible is used as evidence for its own claim.
The believer accepts this by the internal witness of the Holy Spirit.
The circularity is unavoidable.
preserved_transitions: Past success → future trust → circular justification
isomorphisms.notes: The mapping is exact. Both are instances of self-referential justification.

isomorphisms.name: Category Error in Critique
isomorphisms.chi_law: Each system's critique of the other commits a category error by judging the other's foundational axiom using its own method.
isomorphisms.physics_process: Incompatible measurement bases in quantum mechanics: measuring position disturbs momentum; using one basis to judge another yields meaningless results.
isomorphisms.theological_phenomenon: The claim that 'science disproves God' is a category error; science tests natural causes, not supernatural ones.
isomorphisms.prediction: Cross-system critiques will always involve a category error if they judge axioms by the other system's method.
physics_process_steps: Choose a quantum system.
Measure position; you lose information about momentum.
Measure momentum; you lose information about position.
Claiming one measurement invalidates the other is a category error.
mapped_text_steps: Science claims to have disproven God.
But science only tests natural causes.
Theology claims faith is the only way.
But faith is acceptance of an axiom, not a scientific claim.
preserved_transitions: Method A → conclusion about domain B → category error
isomorphisms.notes: Perfect mapping. Both critiques are structurally identical category errors.

isomorphisms.name: Level Playing Field
isomorphisms.chi_law: Both systems are foundational and cannot be externally validated; the debate is about which axiom explains more of reality.
isomorphisms.physics_process: Gauge invariance in physics: different gauge choices lead to equivalent descriptions; the choice is not dictated by the system itself but by empirical adequacy.
isomorphisms.theological_phenomenon: The playing field is level: neither system has epistemic high ground; the question is explanatory power.
isomorphisms.prediction: The debate will shift from 'faith vs. evidence' to 'which axiom explains more.'
physics_process_steps: Choose a gauge (e.g., Coulomb gauge, Lorenz gauge).
The physics is equivalent; the choice is conventional.
Empirical adequacy determines which gauge is useful for a given problem.
mapped_text_steps: Choose a foundational axiom (causal closure or divine revelation).
Both are unprovable from outside.
The question is which accounts for more of what we observe.
preserved_transitions: Choice of axiom → no external validation → comparison by explanatory power
missing_transitions: Gauge choices are equivalent in physics; the two worldviews are not equivalent in content.
broken_correspondences: Gauge invariance implies no empirical difference; the two worldviews have different empirical predictions.
isomorphisms.notes: The mapping is suggestive but not exact. The gauge analogy breaks down because the two systems are not empirically equivalent. However, the structural point about level playing field is valid.
